# Cito PDF

> Cito PDF is a free, open-source Chrome extension (Manifest V3, Apache-2.0) that replaces Chrome's built-in PDF viewer with a research-focused reader built on pdf.js. It streams PDFs so the first page opens before the download finishes, shows a Google Scholar popup for every in-text citation (abstract, Cited by, Cite in APA/MLA/Chicago/BibTeX, Save to library), and is optimised to stay fast on low-memory and dual-core machines. Night mode and AMOLED black, vector printing, no tracking.

Name: Cito PDF ("cito" is Latin for "swiftly, at once"; sounds like "cite").
Author: Ghaleb Aldoboni. Repository: https://github.com/GhalebAldoboni/citopdf
Install: download the release zip, chrome://extensions, Developer mode, Load unpacked.

## Key facts
- Streaming: first request is a 1 MB byte range; pages in view are fetched first, the rest downloads in the background. 200 MB PDF: first page in 0.35 s. 7 MB paper on a 2 MB/s link: 0.55 s instead of 4.5 s.
- Citation popups: Google Scholar PDF Reader's analyzer, run in a worker; a 39-page paper with 276 references is fully linked 3 s after opening. Works on streamed, publisher-hosted and local files, and per paper inside journal issues.
- Performance: 61 fps pinch zoom with one render per gesture; no renders during a fling; text layers only for visible pages; off-screen pages cost nothing; device profile for 4 GB or dual-core machines; rendered pages released after 5 minutes in a hidden tab (JS heap 90 MB to 26 MB).
- Also: keeps the PDF's real URL in the address bar, opens IEEE/ACM/Wiley/arXiv/ProQuest/EBSCO and file:// PDFs, day/night/AMOLED modes, vector printing through Chrome's engine, no analytics.

## Compared with
- Chrome PDF viewer: streams but has no citation popups, no night mode, no device adaptation.
- Google Scholar PDF Reader: citation popups, but a second viewer on top of Chrome's, buffers whole files, closed source.
- Stock pdf.js viewer: open source, but downloads whole files first, raster printing, no citation features.
